digest.component_or_area: compaction sweep and tracker store durability
propositions: A detached compaction worker that dies or races between snapshot rename and git commit leaves the shared tracker working tree dirty with tracked deletions and untracked snapshot files, causing reconverge to abort with 'local changes would be overwritten' and stranding ticket commits.
The fold operation (snapshot-write, retire-rename, git commit) lacks atomicity and rollback; no recovery mechanism exists for abandoned partial folds at startup or next sweep entry.

An intent journal written before any mutation allows recovery to discriminate landed folds (snapshot in HEAD, discard journal), abandoned partial folds (incomplete artifacts, revert and clean), and superseded folds (snapshot gone, clear journal without touching files).

Transient git faults during recovery probes must be distinguished from snapshot-absent conditions to prevent mis-classifying a transient failure as 'snapshot absent' and incorrectly reverting a landed fold.
Incomplete rollback (a reverse-rename failure during abort) must retain the uncommitted snapshot as SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT for fsck repair rather than delete it and lose folded events.
Per-ticket commits inside the sweep (instead of batch stage-and-commit) bound the dirty window to a single fold; recovery at sweep entry cleans abandoned journals before processing the next ticket.
